subject: Vendor chain change notice — FinchCorp subcontracting + DPA alignment
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Raval <anna@blueish.ai>, FinchCorp Contracts <contracts@finchcorp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 27 May 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Vendor chain change notice — FinchCorp subcontracting + DPA alignment

Hi Anna / Finch contracts team,

Thanks for the call earlier. As discussed, FinchCorp is engaging a third party (Blueish AI) to provide a feature-level enrichment service that will touch token-level telemetry for deduped examples. That triggers a subprocessor/flow-down review on our side.

Attached is a proposed subprocessor matrix and the latest SOW redline (Finch_SOW_v3_redline.docx), plus the MSA sections we expect to update (see Redlined_MSA_sections_5-7.docx). Our Legal has flagged two specific asks:

- Standard flow-down of the DPA obligations to any subcontractor doing processing on customer data (confidentiality, data subject rights, breach notification).
- An audit/inspection right limited to scheduled reviews with 30 days' notice and reasonable scope.

Operational constraints to note: for customers needing Private deployment, we require assurance that any subcontractor will accept restrictions on key management (no external KMS keys without prior approval).

Could you confirm (a) the full list of subvendors Blueish will use for FinchCorp work, (b) whether Blueish accepts the DPA flow-down language (we attached DPA_Blueish_SIGNABLE.pdf for quick review), and (c) if there are any anticipated procurement steps on Finch's side (e.g., separate vendor questionnaires)?

If helpful, I can set a 30-minute sync early next week to walk Legal through the flowdown language.

Thanks,

Jonas Weber
Head of Sales, East
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Vendor chain change notice — FinchCorp subcontracting + DPA alignment

Jonas — thanks for the summary and the materials.

A few quick items from our side:

1) Blueish is proposing to subcontract a small ML ops partner ("VectorLabs") for model fine-tuning — they handle feature pipelines only, no persistent storage of PII. We still need to confirm whether VectorLabs will accept the DPA flow-down.

2) Our procurement/legal team will run the attached redlines against our standard SOW. We generally accept audit rights but prefer to limit them to scoping calls and written evidence unless there is a suspected incident.

3) Timeline: Procurement will baseline the license/order terms by next Wed (6/2). If we need further negotiation on Sections 5–7, expect an additional 3–5 business days.

I'll loop in our lead contract reviewer if anything materially changes.

Thanks — Sophie
Sophie Legrand
Senior Commercial Counsel, FinchCorp

Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Vendor chain change notice — FinchCorp subcontracting + DPA alignment

Team — quick legal read and proposed fallback language.

Summary of issues we need to resolve before finalizing Order Form/SOW:

- Flow-down scope: we need the DPA obligations to apply to any subprocessor that performs processing on behalf of Blueish in support of FinchCorp. Proposed clause: "Supplier shall require each subprocessor to enter into written obligations no less protective than those set forth in this Agreement, including data subject rights and breach notification." (see attached redline).

- Audit: propose defining "audit" as "review of written policies, logs and one remote interview with an ops lead, limited to data processing activities relevant to FinchCorp, with 30 days' notice." That preserves our ability to verify compliance while keeping it operationally reasonable.

- KMS / key control: add an explicit prohibition on sharing customer-managed KMS keys with subcontractors unless Customer consents in writing.

Action items for Sales/OPS:

1) Jonas — confirm with Blueish whether VectorLabs will accept the flow-down clause (or whether Blueish will accept responsibility and guarantee compliance).
2) Dev — confirm whether we can support a limited remote audit scope operationally (logs retention window, what evidence we can share).
3) Lauren — line up the SOW/Order Form update to reflect the proposed wording so procurement can attach to the deal.

Attachments: Redlined_MSA_sections_5-7.docx; Finch_SOW_v3_redline.docx

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Laura / team — short ops note:

- We can support the limited remote audit as proposed. We typically retain request logs for 90 days; we can surface anonymized KV cache samples and processing flow diagrams after redaction.
- KMS: we cannot allow external subcontractors to hold customer-managed keys. If Finch requires customer KMS usage, Blueish cannot share keys; they must operate under a model where keys are held in the customer's account or via a supported gateway.
- Timeline: if VectorLabs signs the flowdown we can complete an internal readiness checklist within 5 business days.

Happy to jump on the call if Finch procurement wants to validate the technical scope.

— Dev
